summary: M5.S1 STREAMING (SSE) Al Agent end-to-end test PASS. Backend: 6/6 pytest cases pass — SSE content-type correct, session/token/done events present, tool intent triggers thinking+tool+token events with tool_used set, second-agency isolation OK, session persistence after stream OK, backwards-compat /chat (non-streaming) still returns JSON with session_id/reply/tool_used, unauthenticated request returns 401. Frontend: plain streaming visibly incremental in AlChatWidget (content length grew 0→101→320→424→544→678 across polling samples, 6 distinct lengths), tool flow shows 'via monthly_performance' badge, Stop button replaces Send while busy and clicking it returns the widget to idle without runtime errors, New-session clears all messages.

minor.issue: Rate-limit check happens BEFORE the stream starts, which is correct — but the secondary stream_message (tool follow-up) is not counted against the 60/h limit (same gap as non-streaming /chat noted in iteration_17).

When history replay fails inside the loop (try/except continues with break), it silently degrades context. Currently best-effort, but no event is emitted to the client to indicate replay degradation. Acceptable for now.

issues: Cursor blink (animate-pulse caret) only renders when busy && content.length>0 — for very short replies that arrive in one burst this may not be perceptible. Not a bug; matches Gemini-3-Flash batching behaviour noted in spec.

critical_code_review_comments: al_agent.py:382-388 — sniff logic flushes the entire buf_str on the first 'not-tool' decision via a single 'token' event, then continues; subsequent deltas are sent one-by-one. Correct, but if the first chunk from Gemini already contains >1KB of text, the user perceives the first 'burst' as non-streamed. Consider re-emitting the buffered content split into ~32-char sub-tokens for smoother UX in burst-prone models.

al_agent.py:430 — secondary stream_message for the tool follow-up uses send_message replay history that was already consumed in phase 1; LlmChat session continuity is not guaranteed and the model may lose the conversation thread. Works today because the follow-up prompt embeds the tool result inline, but is fragile.

al_agent.py:455 — final_reply persistence uses ''.join(final_buf) only when tool path runs; in the plain-text path (looks_like_tool=False) final_reply = raw_reply (correct) but if looks_like_tool is None (very short reply path at line 405-408) final_reply is also raw_reply — verified consistent.

AlChatWidget.jsx:97-101 — SSE frame parsing finds the FIRST line starting with 'data:' per frame; if a frame contains multiple data: lines (multi-line SSE), only the first is parsed. Current backend never emits multi-line data, so safe in practice but worth noting.

AlChatWidget.jsx:60-72 — fetch uses credentials:'include' (correct for cookie auth) but no Authorization header fallback; if the user's session cookie is missing the stream silently 401s and the catch shows generic error. Acceptable since same pattern as /chat.

success_rate.frontend: 100% (plain stream incremental, tool badge visible, Stop aborts, New-session clears)
